In review of the refactor that removed Fintype from FintypeCat, it was suggested that it should be renamed as a follow-up:

@Christian Merten said

: Do you also want to rename FintypeCat to say FiniteTypeCat? FintypeCat is a bit misleading with the new implementation.

@Dagur Asgeirsson [said](hhttps://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/36498#discussion_r2922959625)

I think FiniteTypeCat is too long. This category is sometimes denoted Fin in informal mathematics, what do you think about FinCat?

In any case, I think a renaming and deprecation PR should be a followup ([source])).

@Joël Riou said

I would also prefer FiniteTypeCat. FinCat could be easily confused with FinCategory.
FinCat sounds to me like it has something to do with Fin, which wouldn't be accurate

Niels Voss said:

FinCat sounds to me like it has something to do with Fin, which wouldn't be accurate

We already have FinCategory (which just means a finite category, essentially), and this has nothing to do with Fin. I also disagree with the point raised on the PR that FinCat can be confused with FinCategory. We have the convention that names ending with Cat are names of specific categories
6 messages were moved here from #mathlib4 > Design of CategoryTheory.Mat_ and CategoryTheory.Mat by Eric Wieser.
